title: Reading from the right
explanation: Hebrew has 22 letters and is read from right to left. The first letter of a word is the one furthest right. The small dots and dashes around the letters show vowels. You will study those at the Vowel Springs. For now, look at the large letters.

workedExamples.note: Start at the right edge. ע (ayin) comes first, ר (resh) is next, and ב (bet) finishes on the left. Read in that order: e-rev.

title: What a word means here
explanation: A word card gives the usual meaning. The line around a word shows which meaning fits that place. Use Understand to say what a word means. The card will be hidden when you answer.

workedExamples.note: In Genesis 1:3 this word names a thing that comes to be: light. It is a noun here, so 'to shine' would be the wrong answer.

title: Five letters that change at the end
explanation: Five letters take a different shape when they end a word: כ becomes ך, מ becomes ם, נ becomes ן, פ becomes ף, and צ becomes ץ. It is the same letter in a different shape. Check the left end of the word, since that is where the word finishes.

workedExamples.note: Kaf ends this word, so it is written ך.
Mem ends this word, so it is written ם.
Nun ends this word, so it is written ן.
Pe ends this word, so it is written ף.
Tsade ends this word, so it is written ץ.
